The plan-change contract this revision would publish (Slice 6, §6).

**Shown because it is pinned.** The pin's module doc argues that showing
a reviewer content their signature does not cover is the wrong direction;
the mirror of that argument is that content the signature *does* cover
must be on the document. An edge list decides who may move where, so a
reviewer approving it unseen is approving an authorization change they
were never shown.

composites.description:
The composite meters this revision would publish (Slice 10 §6).

Shown for the same reason as the two above and stated because it was
**hashed and not shown for one commit** (D-259): the pin covers the
formula since v11, so a reviewer's signature covers a weighting they were
never displayed — which is precisely the signature they did not give. The
module's invariant is "exactly the fields the pin hashes and no others".

oneOf.description: The billing descriptor set.

entitlement_grants.description:
The entitlement grant set this revision would publish (Slice 6, §6).

Shown for the change contract's reason: it is pinned, so a reviewer's
signature covers it, and a signature over unseen entitlements is one the
reviewer did not give.

oneOf.description: The recurring frequency, interval and all.

period_floor_caps.description:
The plan-level period floor/cap this revision would publish (S2 §6,
**D-319**).

Shown for the three above's reason, and it is the one with the most
direct money consequence: the pin covers it since v14, so a reviewer's
signature covers a minimum charge they were never displayed — and unlike
a price row, a period floor changes what a subscriber pays without
appearing as a line on the invoice that would explain it.

plan_name.description:
The plan's human label (D-318).

**Shown**, because the pin frames it: a rename is a change to what the
catalog will call this plan, a reviewer's signature covers it, and the
module doc above makes showing-or-not an explicit decision rather than an
omission.

plan_tier_override.description:
Whether the tier diverges from the parent SKU's under an audited
override.

rows.description: The candidate row set this publish would produce.

sku_id.description:
The catalog SKU this revision binds. Hashed, because a
rebind inside the approve→commit window would otherwise re-derive to the
same digest.

windows.description:
The window plane the pin covers, one entry per canonical scope key.

Hashed here, for the reason
`sku_id` is: a field inside the digest and outside this document is a field
a reviewer is told `content_matches_pin: false` about while looking at a
page that does not contain it. Two plans differing **only** in their window
intervals rendered byte-identical here and hashed differently.

share_bp.description: What the operator authored, in basis points.

PinnedRevShareGroupView.description: One rev-share group of the pinned composition — the vendor payout split.

parties.description: The parties and their typed shares, in basis points.

platform_cut_bp.description: The group's explicit platform cut, in basis points.

vendor_sku_id.description: The included vendor SKU whose revenue this group allocates.

PinnedThresholdPolicyView.description:
Exactly the threshold-policy version the pin hashes — the reviewer's document
for a D-10 unit.

A **second** pinned-content member rather than a widening of
[`PinnedContentView`], for the reason `PinnedSubject` is a sum type: the two
subjects share no field, and a single view carrying the union of both would
have every member `null` for one of the two kinds. A reviewer would then be
reading a document whose shape does not say what they are approving, and the
exhaustive-destructure guard below would have nothing to be exhaustive over.

effective_from.description: When its thresholds start applying, once approved.

entries.description: The per-currency entries, in the order the pin frames them.

version.description: Which version of the tenant's policy this proposal is.

PinnedWindowsView.description:
One canonical scope key's window set, as the pinned document renders it.

The interval rendering is [`WindowIntervalView`] — `GET …/coverage`'s own, not
a second spelling of it — and the key is [`ScopeKeyView`], the authoring
plane's, which is what [`PriceRowView`] shows a reviewer a few lines above. A
second rendering of one fact is a second answer to it.

What it does **not** carry is a coverage end or a gap list: those are *derived*
from the intervals, the pin frames the intervals, and a document showing a
reviewer a derivation their signature does not cover is the failure this whole
view exists to avoid. `GET …/coverage` is where the derived answers live.

intervals.description: The key's intervals, in the order the pin frames them.

scope_key.description: The ten axes the windows are filed under.

PlanChangeContractRequest.description:
The plan-change contract on the wire.

`request, response` rather than `request`, because
[`PlanShapeRequest`] is both and a member of a response DTO has to be
serializable too.

allowed_change_targets.description:
Explicit published `planId`s. **Omit the field entirely** to state the
fail-safe — no self-service change (`inst-pc-failsafe`) — which is not
the same as sending an empty list.

usage_counter_on_plan_change.description:
`reset` (default) | `carry`. Omitted is `reset`, which is D-113's
ratified default and the safe direction.

PlanChangeContractView.description: The plan-change contract as a reviewer sees it (Slice 6, §6).

allowed_change_targets.description:
The explicit published `planId`s a self-service change may travel to.
**Absent means no self-service change** (`inst-pc-failsafe`), which is a
value with a reading and not a missing field; an empty list is an author
who stated the set and left it empty, and the two are kept apart.

PlanCoverageView.description: The plan's whole time axis, one entry per canonical scope key.

keys.description:
Every key: the ones a billable row sits on, and the ones only windows
mention. Ordered by the key's canonical rendering, so two reads of one
state read identically.

plan_id.description: The plan the report is about.

PlanPhaseView.description: One phase of a revision's phase chain.

converts_to_phase_id.description: The phase this one converts into; `null` on the terminal phase.

display_trial_days.description: The trial length a storefront displays, on a `trial` phase.

phase_duration_days.description: How long the phase lasts; `null` on the terminal phase.

phase_id.description:
Stable across revisions (D-83): the `phase` scope-key axis is filed under
it, so a copy-forward keeps the id rather than minting a new one.

PlanSellabilityView.description: The plan's sellability on one market at one instant.

at.description:
The instant the answer is about — the caller's own, echoed so a stored
response cannot be mistaken for one about a different moment.

catalog_version.description:
The pin-eligible version the answer was read from, `null` when none carries
this plan.

currency.description: The currency half of the bound market.

keys.description:
Every key the purchase binds on this market, eligibility-resolved.
**Empty means not sellable**, never vacuously sellable.

region.description: The region half of the bound market.

verdict.description:
The D-94 conjunction: `sellable` | `not_sellable` | `not_evaluable`.

**`not_evaluable` is not a yes.** With two of the six predicates unanswerable
by any version this gear can project, it is what a fully-covered, in-dates,
published plan answers today: the gate saying it is not yet a gate.

PlanShapeRequest.description:
The plan shape a create authors, and the one facet a `PATCH` may move.

Every member is optional because a plan is assembled over several calls: the
shape rules run at **publish**, not at save, so an unfinished draft is a
legal draft (§4.2 step 2).

available_from.description: Start of the availability window, UTC.

available_to.description: End of the availability window, UTC.

oneOf.description:
The plan-change contract (Slice 6, §6): the published `planId`s a
self-service change may travel to, the comparability rank that
classifies one, and D-113's tier-`Q` continuity flag.

Sent **whole or not at all**, which is the shape
[`PlanShapePatch::change_contract`] gives it: K4 ties the rank to whether
the edge list names anyone, so a caller able to move one member alone
could express a state no publish accepts.

The entitlement grant set (Slice 6, §6, D-41): the plan-level feature
flags and quotas, the `PlanTier` they resolved from when they did, and
any per-phase sets keyed by `phaseId`.

Sent **whole or not at all**, for the change contract's reason below.
The recurring frequency, interval and all.

plan_name.description:
The plan's human label (D-318). Free text an operator chose, distinct
from the tier, which is a classification the catalog reasons about.

Absent leaves it alone; the empty string is **refused**, not stored, so
`NULL` stays the only spelling of "unnamed".

plan_tier.description: The plan's tier (a registry-owned taxonomy, so a free string).

plan_tier_override.description: Declare or withdraw the audited tier override (P3).

sku_id.description: Bind the plan to a catalog SKU.

PlanSummaryView.description:
One plan on a page: the revision an author is holding, and nothing that costs
a query of its own.

The five child sets [`PlanView`] carries are each a query of their own, so
rendering them a hundred times for a catalogue screen would be six hundred
round trips to show a tier and a state. A caller opens
`GET …/plans/{planId}` for the rest — the split
`list_approvals` / `get_approval` already make one module over.

available_from.description: Start of the availability window, UTC.

available_to.description: End of the availability window, UTC.

created_at_utc.description: When the revision was created, UTC.

plan_id.description: The plan this revision belongs to.

plan_name.description: The plan's human label (D-318), absent until an operator names it.

plan_tier.description: The plan's tier (a registry-owned taxonomy, so a string).

revision.description:
The revision number the page is answering about — the open draft's when
the plan has one, else the current revision's.

row_version.description:
The precondition a caller needs to `PATCH` this row without reading it
again. Carried on the page for the same reason [`PlanView`] carries it: a
client that cannot see response headers can still submit an `If-Match`.

sku_id.description: The catalog SKU this plan realizes, when one is bound.

PlanView.description:
One plan revision, whole: its own columns and its five child sets.

The child sets are here rather than on sub-resources of their own because
S2 §5's `PATCH` cell names those facets as the plan's shape - a read
that omitted them could not round-trip a patch, and an author would have to
guess what a `PATCH` was about to replace.

available_from.description: Start of the availability window, UTC.

available_to.description: End of the availability window, UTC.

change_contract.description:
The revision's plan-change contract (Slice 6, §6).

Here for [`PlanView::entitlement_grants`]' reason, and it carries one
distinction the round trip depends on: `allowed_change_targets` is `null`
for the fail-safe and `[]` for an author who cleared their edges, and the
two are different states of the same plan.

composites.description:
The revision's derived (composite) meter set, in the store's order.

**A write surface whose read surface does not show the value is half a
feature**, and here it is load-bearing rather than symmetric-for-tidiness:
the `composites` facet replaces the set wholesale, and
[`CompositeMeterRequest::composite_id`] is what preserves a definition's
identity across such a replace. An author with no way to read the ids back
could only ever re-mint them, and D-106's stable id would hold for the
copy-forward and break for every edit.

An empty list is a revision that defines no composite, which is the ordinary
case: unlike [`PlanView::descriptor_set`] there is no attached-but-empty
state to keep apart from absence, because the set is rows and not a row.

created_at_utc.description: When the revision was created, UTC.

created_by.description: Pseudonymous principal id of the authoring actor.

oneOf.description: The revision's descriptor set, or `null` when none is attached.

entitlement_grants.description:
The revision's entitlement grant set (Slice 6, §6, D-41).

A write surface whose read surface does not show the value is half a
feature, for the third time on this view and with the sharpest version of
the argument: the `shape` facet's `entitlement_grants` member is **sent
whole or not at all**, so an author adding one quota has to resubmit the
flags, the tier reference and every per-phase set beside it. Without a
surface that answers them the
`PATCH` accepted the set, the create stored it, the pin hashed it and
`approvals::PinnedContentView` showed it to a *reviewer*, and the author
who wrote it could not read it back.

It is the [`EntitlementGrantsRequest`] twin and not
`approvals::EntitlementGrantsView`, which is the split the module doc
states: the reviewer's view renders the **resolved** per-phase map, and
this is the authoring plane, where what an author needs answered is what
they may send back.

oneOf.description: The recurring frequency, interval and all.

lifecycle_state.description:
`draft` | `abandoned` | `published` | `superseded` | `retired`. Named on
the wire so a caller never has to infer which revision it was given.

period_floor_caps.description:
The revision's period floor/cap set, in `(currency, region)` order
(**D-319**).

A write surface whose read surface does not show the value is half a
feature, and here the read is what makes a wholesale replace usable at
all: the facet replaces the set, so an author adding a bound in a second
market has to be able to read the first one back to resubmit it.

An empty list is a plan with no minimum, which is the ordinary plan.

phases.description: The revision's phase chain, in the order the store returns.

plan_id.description: The plan this revision belongs to.

plan_name.description: The plan's human label (D-318), absent until an operator names it.

plan_tier.description: The plan's tier (a registry-owned taxonomy, so a string).

plan_tier_override.description:
Whether the tier diverges from the parent SKU's under an audited
override.

revision.description:
The revision number. An **identity, not a counter** (D-145): the sequence
may have gaps where a draft was abandoned.

row_version.description:
The revision's optimistic-concurrency version - the same number the
`ETag` header quotes, carried in the body too so a client that cannot see
response headers can still submit a precondition.

sku_id.description: The catalog SKU this plan realizes, when one is bound.

PluginDto.description: Response DTO for a plugin (reserved for follow-up implementation)

allowed_mime_types.description: Allowed MIME types for upload (empty = all types permitted at this level).

enabled_event_types.description: Enabled `EventBroker` event types (empty = none at this level).

PolicyDto.description: A stored policy row as returned by `GET /policy`.

PostInvoiceRequestDto.description:
The `POST /journal-entries` request body: a fully-recognized invoice
(Variant A) to post. The target seller ledger is the body's own `tenant_id`
(tenant in body, not path — the vhp-core REST convention); the `(entry,
post)` PEP gate authorizes it.

correlation_id.description:
Caller-supplied trace token propagated onto the entry (NOT an authority
claim — the poster identity is the authenticated subject, stamped
server-side, never read from the body).

due_date.description:
AR due date stamped on the AR line (drives AR-aging); `None` ⇒ due on
posting.

period_id.description: The fiscal `period_id` (`YYYYMM`) the entry posts into.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this posts into (= `entry.tenant_id`);
the PEP gate target. Carried in the body, not the path.

PostInvoiceResponseDto.description:
The `POST /journal-entries` (invoice-post) response: the posted-entry
reference (`entry_id`, `created_seq`, `replayed`) plus the recognition
schedules materialized in the SAME transaction (`schedules`, empty when the
invoice carried no deferred items). Extends the bare posting reference with
the discovery half of the recognition-schedule surface — the minted
`schedule_id`s are otherwise only observable on the event bus. On an
idempotent replay (`replayed = true`) the schedules are those the original
post materialized.

PostingPolicyResponse.description:
The written posting-policy version (the minted `version` + the values it
carries; the resolver picks the latest `effective_from`).

effective_from.description: The instant this version takes effect.

version.description: The minted version (`max + 1`, `0` for the first).

PostingPolicyView.description:
The tenant's effective posting policy (read-surface) — the configured version
in force, or the gear defaults when the tenant has set none.

PostingRefDto.description:
Reference to a posted (or idempotently replayed) entry. `replayed` is `true`
when the call matched a prior post (the handler then renders `200`, not
`201`).

Predicate.description: A predicate comparing a resource property to a value or subquery.

oneOf.description: Equality: `resource_property = value`
Set membership: `resource_property IN (values)`

allOf.description: Group membership: `resource_property IN (SELECT resource_id FROM membership WHERE group_id IN (group_ids))`

oneOf.description: Group membership: `resource_property IN (SELECT resource_id FROM membership WHERE group_id IN (group_ids))`

allOf.description: Group subtree: `resource_property IN (SELECT resource_id FROM membership WHERE group_id IN (SELECT descendant_id FROM closure WHERE ancestor_id IN (ancestor_ids)))`

oneOf.description: Group subtree: `resource_property IN (SELECT resource_id FROM membership WHERE group_id IN (SELECT descendant_id FROM closure WHERE ancestor_id IN (ancestor_ids)))`

allOf.description: Tenant subtree: `resource_property IN (SELECT descendant_id FROM tenant_closure WHERE ancestor_id = root_tenant_id)`

oneOf.description: Tenant subtree: `resource_property IN (SELECT descendant_id FROM tenant_closure WHERE ancestor_id = root_tenant_id)`

PredicateAnswerView.description:
One predicate's answer, as the wire renders it.

**`answer` is a token and there is no boolean anywhere in this document**, which
is D-99 reaching the wire: what a consumer is given is intervals, states, a
derived coverage end and per-predicate tokens, so no field of it is an answer to
a question about the reader's clock.

`detail` and `owed_to` are both nullable and never both set: the first belongs to
`failed` and the second to `not_evaluable`. Two fields rather than one, because
the whole of D-167 clause (3) is that a consumer can tell *"this predicate is
false"* from *"this version cannot evaluate this predicate"* — and one merged
message field would have made the difference a matter of reading English.

detail.description: Why the predicate is false, on `failed` and nowhere else.

ordinal.description: The design set's own number for the predicate, 1 to 6.

owed_to.description:
What owes the fact this predicate reads, on `not_evaluable` and nowhere
else — the slice, or the version.

amount_minor.description:
The base list amount in minor units.

NULL on a row whose money is a **rate** — see [`Self::unit_rate_nano_minor`].

catalog_version.description:
The catalog version the answer was resolved at, so a caller can pin what
they were shown.

display_trial_days.description: The trial days a consumer surface shows, when the plan declares any.

not_sellable_ga.description:
C3's gate: authorable and **previewable**, but not sellable on this
market until Tax Engine GA. Carried because §2 explicitly permits the
preview of a gated row — a caller has to be able to tell the two apart.

resolved_tax_category.description: D-154's resolved effective tax category, as the version froze it.

tax_inclusive.description: Whether that amount is tax-inclusive (§2's success scenario).

tier_band_count.description:
§2's **tier summary**: how many tier bands this market's rows carry, or
`None` when none do.

A count rather than the bands themselves — a full band table is what
`GET …/prices` is for. It exists because a tiered or usage-priced market
has **no** single `amountMinor`, so without it §2's success scenario is
unanswerable for exactly the plans whose pricing is most worth previewing.

unit_rate_nano_minor.description:
The base list **rate**, in nano-minor units, for the rows that price from
one.

D-311 gave `per_unit` the pair `(wants_amount = false, wants_rate = true)`:
a per-seat row's money lives here and its `amount_minor` is NULL *by rule*,
so a view carrying only the amount quotes such a plan no price at all. That
is the modal subscription shape — recurring, `per_unit`, seat-counted.

A member of its own rather than folded into `amount_minor`, because folding
them is exactly the conflation D-311 removed, and because a consumer reading
a nano-minor rate as a minor amount is wrong by a factor of a billion.

PriceContentView.description:
Everything about a row an open draft may still change.

It is a whole-content submission and not a patch, for the reason
[`PriceContent`]'s own doc gives: a price row's fields are not independent of
each other — moving `model_kind` from `graduated` to `flat` has to drop the
band set and set `amount_minor` in the *same* write, because every
intermediate state is one no Slice-3 rule can pass.

aggregation_function.description: How the in-window quantity is derived (D-44).

aggregation_granularity.description: The granule a non-`sum` window is cut into (D-44).

amount_minor.description: The row's own amount, on the kinds that carry one.

anchor_day.description:
The day a `fixed_day` policy anchors on, 1–31. Refused beside any other
policy, and required beside `fixed_day`.

bands.description: The band set, ordered by lower bound on read.

billing_anchor_policy.description:
Where the subscription's cycle boundary falls: `calendar_month` |
`subscription_start` | `fixed_day` (K2). Required on a recurring row
together with the two below.

billing_timing.description: `advance` | `arrears` — Slice-6-owned, so a free string here.

credit_on_downgrade.description: Whether a downgrade off this row is credit-eligible.

dimension_key.description:
The priced dimension within the meter; absent on a whole-meter line, as
it is on the scope key this row's view carries beside it.

Emitted as `null` for that absence and **accepted** as `null`, as the
empty string, or omitted — all three decode to the same undimensioned
line, so a client echoing back a body this surface issued round-trips
whichever spelling it holds.

grandfather_until.description:
The grandfathering horizon. Only an `existing_grandfathered` row may
carry one.

oneOf.description: The plan-scoped included allowance (D-45).

manual_quantity.description: The manual quantity, on a `manual` source.

max_hold_granules.description: The `maxHold` bound on a non-`sum` row.

meter.description: The meter a usage row prices.

min_qty_usage_fallback.description:
What happens beneath the usage floor; launch: `exception`
(`inst-ft-fallback`).

model_kind.description:
`flat` | `per_unit` | `graduated` | `volume` | `package`. Authored, never
inferred — there is no implicit default at rating time.

quantity_source.description: Where a non-usage `per_unit` row's quantity comes from.

reserved_rate_nano_minor.description:
The reserved rate, in the row's currency (`inst-rv-attrs`).

This field and the five below it are Slice 10's authoring surface, and
they are on **this** view rather than one of their own because
`inst-ad-author` says so: primitives "author through the Slice 2/3
plan/price PATCH surfaces", row-attached ones on the price row. S10 §5
declares no endpoint of its own for the same reason.

rounding_policy_ref.description: The named rounding policy this row resolves against.

supersedes_price_id.description: The predecessor this row supersedes on its key.

tax_category_ref.description:
The row's tax category (D-110) — the **source of truth**, and the only
place one lives. Absent states none, and D-154 then resolves the region
taxonomy's default at publish; it is not the same as "no category".

tax_inclusive.description: Whether the authored amounts are tax-inclusive. Absent is `false`.

unit_rate_nano_minor.description:
The `per_unit` **rate**, in 10^-9 ISO-4217 minor units (D-311).

Its own member rather than a second meaning for `amount_minor`, which
carried the `flat` sum *and* the `per_unit` price — an invoice amount and
a multiplier under one name. A `per_unit` row sets this and leaves
`amount_minor` absent.

created_at_utc.description: When the row was authored, UTC.

created_by.description: Pseudonymous principal id of the authoring actor.

price_id.description: The row's identity, minted by the surface at creation.

row_version.description:
The row's own optimistic-concurrency version — never the plan's (D-141),
and the same number the `ETag` quotes.

scope_key.description: The ten axes it is filed under.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem+json. `context` varies by error category.

ProposedActView.description:
The act a window unit is being decided on, for the reviewer's read.

A projection of [`crate::infra::window::ProposedAct`], which is parsed from the
record's own subject. Instants are rendered as the subject spells them rather
than re-parsed: the subject is the authenticated artifact, and a re-parse that
normalised an offset would show a reviewer something other than what was signed.

current_effective_to.description:
The end as it stands before the act; `null` for a schedule, and for a window
that is already open-ended.

effective_from.description: The start a schedule proposes; `null` for the other two.

effective_to.description: The end the act proposes; `null` means open-ended.

price_id.description: The price row a schedule would put a window on; `null` for the other two acts.

window_id.description: The window the act is on; `null` for a schedule, whose window does not exist yet.

ProvisioningRequestDto.description:
The provisioning request body: the target seller tenant, accounts, currency
scales, and the fiscal-calendar config to seed in one transaction. The
tenant is carried in the **body** (not the path) — the gear's REST surface is
tenant-from-context/body per the vhp-core convention (RBAC/RMS), and a
provision targets a seller the caller authorizes via the PEP gate.

ProvisioningResultDto.description:
The provisioning result: the accounts THIS call created + per-grain
created-vs-existing counts.

PspSettlementReportRequest.description:
`POST /ledger/control/psp-settlement-report` request body: the PSP's net settled
amount for `(tenant, period)`.

settled_minor.description: Net settled amount in minor units the PSP reports (net of refunds/returns).

tenant_id.description: The seller tenant whose ledger this feeds; the PEP gate target. In the body.

PublishAcceptedView.description:
What a publish answers with — which of the two acts it performed, and why.

`response` only, as `overlays::SubmitAcceptedView` is: it carries an
[`ApprovalView`], which is a projection of a stored record and has no
`Deserialize`. It was declared `request, response` while its fields were three
scalars, and nothing ever sent one.

oneOf.description:
The unit this call opened, on the submit arm; the unit that authorized it,
on the publish arm.

bundle_id.description: The bundle this call acted on.

materiality.description:
Why this change is material — **evaluated, not asserted**.

It reads `alwaysMaterialTrigger` for every composition change (D-104), and
that constancy is a property of the rule rather than of this field: the
token is produced by [`bundle_publish_materiality`] through the same
evaluator every other unit's is. A hard-coded literal here tells a client a
property of the request that nothing has established, and a false token cannot
be told from a real one downstream.

outcome.description:
Which act this was: `submitted_for_approval` on the first call,
`published` on the call a second principal's approval authorized.

D-104 makes a composition change always material, so the first call over
any content **stages** it. `POST …/price-overlays/{id}/submit` answers the
same two-token shape for the same reason.

markets.description:
The `(currency, region)` markets the bundle sells in.

Supplied rather than derived because a `sum_of_parts` bundle carries no
price rows of its own (`inst-bb-rowless`), so there is nothing to read the
market set off. It is the coverage walk's domain and the tax-basis walk's.

PublishOutcomeView.description:
What the call did: opened a unit, or froze the revision.

One response type across both statuses rather than two schemas on one
operation, so a generated client has one thing to deserialize and reads
`outcome` to know which arm it got.

oneOf.description: The unit this call opened, or the one it published under.

The evaluator's verdict. Present on both arms — a publish that ran under
an approval says what made the change material in the first place.
The receipt, on the publish arm.

PublishReceiptView.description: What a publish commit produced (§4.2 step 4's five artifacts, named).

audit_seq.description: The `seq` the plan's audit-chain segment reached.

pending_version_ref.description:
The registry's **pending** handle. It is not a `CatalogVersion` and must
not be pinned as one: the commit requests an assignment and
`CatalogVersionPublished` resolves it, so a consumer that treated this as
a version would be resolving against an addressability that does not
exist yet.

published_price_ids.description: The price rows this commit moved into `published`.

PullRefDto.description:
GitHub-shaped `head`/`base` of a pull request: the branch name plus the
commit it pointed at. Distinct from [`GitRefDto`], which is the
commit-only shape branches and tags use.

ref.description: Branch name, under GitHub's own key.

node_id.description: GitHub's GraphQL global id, as GitHub itself returns it.

oneOf.description:
Who opened it, who it is assigned to, who was asked to review, and
the labels it carries.

PullRequestFileDto.description: GitHub-shaped changed file of a pull request.

patch.description: The file's unified diff, as GitHub returns it on this endpoint.

PullRequestMarkerDto.description:
Marker object GitHub attaches to issues that are pull requests.

The braces are load-bearing: serde serializes a braced empty struct as
`{}` (GitHub's marker shape) but a unit struct as `null`.

PutAddressReq.description: REST DTO for creating/upserting an address

PutCustomerGroupTaxonomyRequest.description: The body of a `PUT`: the complete value set.

values.description:
The whole taxonomy, not a patch. A value declared today and absent here
is **retired**.

PutRoundingPoliciesRequest.description: The body of a `PUT`: the complete value set, not a patch.

values.description:
The whole vocabulary. A value declared today and absent here is
**retired**, and the retirement is refused while anything names it.

PutTaxonomyRequest.description: The body of a `PUT`: the complete value set.

values.description:
The whole taxonomy, not a patch. A value declared today and absent here is
**retired**.

PutTenantMetadataDto.description:
Request body for `PUT /tenants/{tenant_id}/metadata/{type_id}`.

The wire shape is the JSON payload to upsert, transmitted in-place
as `TenantMetadataValue` (`type: object, additionalProperties: true`
per `OpenAPI`). No metadata fields cross the request envelope -- the
chained `type_id` is the path parameter, not part of the body.

value.description:
GTS-schema-validated metadata payload. The service rejects
`null` (`DomainError::Validation`) before any state read.

effective_from.description:
When the thresholds start applying, once approved. UTC, millisecond
precision (D-144). Required on a threshold proposal; **must be absent on a
retirement**, which is not schedulable — see `retire`.

entries.description:
The per-currency entries. **The whole policy**, not a patch: a version is a
complete entry set, so a currency left out of this list is a currency with
no threshold — which is material by `inst-mat-percurrency`'s fail-safe
rather than a currency that keeps its old value. Required on a threshold
proposal; **must be absent on a retirement**.

retire.description:
Propose the **tombstone** — a version that positively says this tenant has
no thresholds (D-185).

A positive marker rather than an empty `entries`, because an empty entry set
writes no rows and no reader could tell it from a version nobody proposed —
which is why the authoring door refuses one. And the same `PUT` rather than
a `DELETE`, because nothing is deleted: the store is append-only, and a
retirement is an **appended version** like any other, minted with the next
number, pinned, and in force only once an independent reviewer approves it.
A verb promising removal would describe the opposite of what happens.

Mutually exclusive with the two fields above: a retirement authors no
entries, and it is not schedulable — it takes the tenant back to *everything
is material*, so a future date would be an operator asking for **less**
review between now and then than they have already decided they want.

QueryAggregatedUsageRecordsRequest.description:
Aggregated-query request body for
`POST /usage-collector/v1/records/aggregate`. The typed `gts_id`, the
`OData` `$filter`, and the `metadata.<key>` side-channel remain query
parameters (mirroring `GET /usage-collector/v1/records`); only the
aggregation spec (operator + group-by dimensions) ships in the body.

QuotaWarning.description: Per-tier, per-period quota warning entry in the SSE `done` event.

next_reset.description:
RFC 3339 timestamp of the next quota-period reset.
Present when `warning` or `exhausted` is true; absent otherwise.

RecognitionInputDto.description:
The optional per-item ASC 606 recognition spec on the wire (Slice 4). Maps to
the domain [`RecognitionInput`]; absence on an item ⇒ no deferral. `timing` is
`"point_in_time"` (no deferral, explicit) or `"straight_line"` (defer the
whole ex-tax amount over `periods` equal segments from `first_period_id`,
defaulted to the invoice period when omitted). The optional refs/flags carry
PO / SSP / VC / subscription context onto the materialized schedule.

first_period_id.description:
Straight-line only: first fiscal period (`YYYYMM`) the schedule recognizes
into; `None` ⇒ defaulted to the invoice period.

immaterial_one_shot_sku.description:
`true` iff the Catalog SKU is flagged immaterial-one-shot-eligible (an R4
exemption precondition). `None` ⇒ `false` (not eligible).

multi_po.description:
`true` for a genuine multi-performance-obligation line — the only case
where a missing/unresolvable SSP snapshot blocks the post (§4.4). `None` ⇒
`false` (single-PO).

periods.description:
Straight-line only: number of equal recognition segments (`>= 1`).
Required for `timing = "straight_line"`, ignored for `"point_in_time"`.

po_allocation_group.description: The PO / allocation group this line books under (audit, §4.7).

policy_ref.description: The deferral+timing policy version stamped immutably on the schedule.

ssp_snapshot_ref.description:
The SSP snapshot ref pinned at contract inception; required + resolvable
for a `multi_po` line (else `SSP_SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED`).

subscription_ref.description: The subscription/entitlement this obligation belongs to (audit).

vc_estimate_ref.description:
Variable-consideration estimate ref (carried only — VC posting is OUT of
the MVP, N-revrec-4).

vc_method_ref.description:
Variable-consideration method ref (carried only — VC posting is OUT of
the MVP, N-revrec-4).

RecognitionRunQueuedResponse.description:
The `POST /recognition-runs` response when the run had to park one or more
out-of-order segments `QUEUED` for a later drain (HTTP 202 Accepted): the run
ran (it may have released in-order segments) but a due segment's lower-period
predecessor was not yet `DONE` (§4.6). `status` is the fixed
`recognition-period-queued` token; `released` + `queued` are this pass's
tallies. A later run drains the `QUEUED` segments once their predecessors
commit. Mirrors `AllocationQueuedResponse`. The `Queued` arm of the outcome.

period_id.description: The period the run was triggered for (`YYYYMM`).

queued.description: Segments parked `QUEUED` this pass (a predecessor period was not `DONE`).

released.description: Segments released in order on this pass before/around the queued ones.

run_id.description: The run that executed (the queued ones are the out-of-order tail).

status.description: Always `recognition-period-queued` (a normal-body kebab-case token, not an error).

RecognitionRunResponse.description:
The `POST /recognition-runs` response when the run EXECUTED (fresh or an
idempotent replay of a prior trigger): the run identity + the release tally.
A fresh run renders `200`, an idempotent replay also `200` (the run already
committed under the original trigger; `replayed = true`). The `Ran` arm of
the outcome.

already_recognized.description: Segments that were already released (an idempotent `RECOGNITION` replay).

period_id.description: The period the run released for (`YYYYMM`).

released.description: Segments released on THIS pass (a fresh `DR CL / CR Revenue` post).

replayed.description:
`true` when this trigger replayed a prior run with the same
`(tenant, run_id)` (no new run row was inserted; no re-release).

run_id.description: The run that executed (minted by the trigger, or replayed).

RecognitionRunView.description:
The `GET /recognition-runs` / `GET /recognition-runs/{run_id}` response: one
recorded ASC 606 recognition run (read-surface R4). Drawn from the
`recognition_run` row (the `(tenant, period_id, run_id)` grain — the run is the
orchestration wrapper that released a period's due segments). `status` is the
run lifecycle (`RUNNING` ⇒ in-flight / `DONE` ⇒ completed / `FAILED` ⇒ aborted);
`started_at_utc` is when the run began. Tenant-scoped (SQL-level BOLA): an
unknown run — or one outside the caller's subtree — yields a `404` (no existence
leak). Mirrors [`DisputeView`].

period_id.description: The fiscal period (`YYYYMM`) the run released due segments for.

RecognitionScheduleListResponse.description:
The `GET /recognition-schedules` response: the recognition schedule headers
matching the `(tenant_id[, invoice_id][, revenue_stream])` filter (segments
omitted — the by-id surface carries those). A discovery surface for the
server-minted `schedule_id`; an empty list is a normal `200`, never a `404`.

truncated.description:
`true` when the result was capped server-side — more schedules exist than
returned (the list surface is not paginated). A client seeing `truncated`
must narrow the filter (`invoice_id` / `revenue_stream`) to see the rest.

RecognitionScheduleResponse.description:
The `GET /recognition-schedules/{schedule_id}` response: one schedule's
lifecycle view (design §3.7 / §4) — the schedule header (status, version,
revenue stream, currency, total-deferred / recognized-to-date, the originating
invoice + the §4.7 item-link anchor, the PO / subscription / policy refs) plus
its segments, ordered by `segment_no` (period order). A schedule outside the
caller's authorized subtree (or simply absent) yields a 404 — never this body
(no existence leak).

po_allocation_group.description: The PO / allocation group this obligation books under; `null` when none.

policy_ref.description: The immutable deferral/timing policy version stamped at build.

revenue_stream.description: The revenue stream the obligation books to (one schedule per stream).

segments.description: The schedule's segments, ordered by `segment_no` (period order).

source_invoice_item_ref.description:
The Contract-liability invoice line the schedule draws down (the §4.7
invoice-link anchor).

subscription_ref.description: The subscription / entitlement this obligation belongs to; `null` when none.

total_deferred_minor.description: The total deferred Contract-liability the schedule plans to release.

version.description: The lineage version (`0` fresh; `old + 1` for a `replace` successor).

RecognitionScheduleSegmentDto.description:
One recognition segment in the `GET /recognition-schedules/{schedule_id}`
response: the `segment_no` (immutable, 1:1 with `period_id`), the period it
recognizes into, its minor-unit amount, and its release status
(`PENDING` | `QUEUED` | `DONE`). A row of [`RecognitionScheduleResponse::segments`].

period_id.description: The fiscal period this segment recognizes into (`YYYYMM`).

RecognitionScheduleSummaryDto.description:
One recognition schedule header in the `GET /recognition-schedules` list
response — like [`RecognitionScheduleResponse`] but WITHOUT segments (the
by-id `GET /recognition-schedules/{schedule_id}` carries those). Maps from
[`bss_ledger_sdk::RecognitionScheduleSummaryView`].

po_allocation_group.description: The PO / allocation group this obligation books under; `null` when none.

policy_ref.description: The immutable deferral/timing policy version stamped at build.

revenue_stream.description: The revenue stream the obligation books to (one schedule per stream).

source_invoice_item_ref.description: The Contract-liability invoice line the schedule draws down.

subscription_ref.description: The subscription / entitlement this obligation belongs to; `null` when none.

total_deferred_minor.description: The total deferred Contract-liability the schedule plans to release.

version.description: The lineage version (`0` fresh; `old + 1` for a `replace` successor).

ReconciliationRunView.description: One reconciliation-run row, projected for the read. PII-free (ids + variance).

RecordDisputePhaseRequest.description:
The `POST /disputes/{dispute_id}/phases` request body: record one phase of a
chargeback dispute. `{dispute_id}` (the dispute's external id) comes from the
PATH; the target seller ledger is the body's own `tenant_id` (tenant in body,
not path — the vhp-core REST convention); the `(dispute, write)` PEP gate
authorizes it. The LEDGER chooses the variant at `opened` from `funds_at_open`
(`"withheld"` ⇒ cash-hold, `"not_moved"` ⇒ AR-reclass); `phase` is one of
`"opened" | "won" | "lost" | "partial"` (Group B implements `opened`).
`cycle` defaults to 1 and increments on a re-open. `invoice_id` is required
for an AR-reclass `opened` (the disputed `(payer, invoice)` grain), ignored
for cash-hold. `scale` is advisory; `effective_at` `None` ⇒ stamped at post
time.

disputed_amount_minor.description:
The disputed amount in minor units (`> 0`): the **gross** claim (what the
buyer paid / the bank reverses), NOT net of the PSP fee — the ledger sizes a
`CASH_HOLD` cash leg at `net = settled − fee` itself.

effective_at.description: Phase instant; `None` ⇒ stamped at post time (current-month period).

funds_at_open.description:
The funds-movement fact: `"withheld"` (card rails) | `"not_moved"`
(invoice/ACH) — read at `opened` to choose the variant.

invoice_id.description:
The disputed `(payer, invoice)` AR grain — required for an AR-reclass
`opened`, ignored for cash-hold.

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this disputes within; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

RecordDisputePhaseResponse.description:
The `POST /disputes/{dispute_id}/phases` response when the phase POSTED
inline: a reference to the dispute phase posting. A fresh phase renders `201`,
an idempotent replay `200` (the handler reads `replayed`).

ReferenceView.description: A reference to the plan, rendered for the confirm screen.

kind.description: What kind of reference it is.

referrer_label.description: A name an operator can act on.

RefundQuarantinedResponse.description:
The `POST /refunds` response when the refund references a payment with no
resolvable origin settlement: the refund was durably QUARANTINED (HTTP 202
Accepted), NOT posted. `status` is the fixed `refund-quarantined` token; `flow`
+ `business_id` are the quarantine queue key and `quarantined_at` the intake
instant. No posting handle — nothing has posted (and de-quarantine re-validates
all §4.7 caps + the then-current D2 threshold + dispute state before any post).
Mirrors [`AllocationQueuedResponse`].

quarantined_at.description: When the intake durably quarantined the request.

status.description: Always `refund-quarantined` (a normal-body kebab-case token, not an error).

RefundRequest.description:
The `POST /refunds` request body: one PSP refund phase to record (the
**money-out** side that unwinds a settled receipt). The target seller ledger
is the body's own `tenant_id` (tenant in body, not path — the vhp-core REST
convention); the `(entry, post)` PEP gate authorizes it (a refund posts a
balanced journal entry into the seller's ledger, like the credit/debit notes,
design §8 / Phase-1 precedent). `pattern` selects the economic shape
(`"A_UNALLOCATED"` / `"B_RESTORE_AR"`); `phase` the lifecycle stage
(`"initiated"` / `"confirmed"` / `"rejected"` / `"voided"` /
`"unknown_final"`). `invoice_id` is required for Pattern B (the AR it
restores), absent for Pattern A. `two_stage` defaults to `true` (the
conservative `REFUND_CLEARING` shape). `relates_to_refund_id` + `direction`
drive a refund-of-refund (Group E); a first-order refund omits both (direction
defaults to outbound). `scale` is advisory; the ledger resolves the
authoritative currency scale.

amount_minor.description: The cash to return, in minor units (`> 0`).

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency (all legs share it; MUST match the origin settlement's).

direction.description:
The economic direction (refund-of-refund only): `OUTBOUND` | `CLAWBACK`.
`None` ⇒ `OUTBOUND` for a first-order refund (the domain default is
claw-back ONLY when a `relates_to_refund_id` is set; a first-order refund is
always outbound, so the DTO defaults to outbound here and lets
`validate_shape` require the link for an explicit claw-back).

invoice_id.description:
The invoice whose AR the refund restores — REQUIRED for Pattern B, MUST be
absent for Pattern A (validated by the domain `validate_shape`).

payer_tenant_id.description: The tenant the refund returns cash to (the original payer).

payment_id.description: The origin settled payment the refund unwinds (NOT NULL both patterns, D7).

psp_refund_id.description: The PSP's refund id — the idempotency grain together with `phase`.

refund_id.description:
The business id of this refund — the `refund` row's surrogate PK +
the `GET /refunds/{refundId}` handle (NOT the idempotency key).

relates_to_refund_id.description:
The prior refund this one references (refund-of-refund link); `None` for a
first-order refund.

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this posts into; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

two_stage.description:
`true` (default) ⇒ the two-stage `REFUND_CLEARING` shape; `false` ⇒ the
single-step shape (D1). `None` ⇒ `true`.

RefundResponse.description:
The `POST /refunds` (and the refund leg of `POST /refund-with-credit-note`)
response when the refund POSTED inline: a reference to the refund-stage
posting. A fresh stage renders `201`, an idempotent replay `200` (the handler
reads `replayed`). Mirrors [`SettlePaymentResponse`].

RefundView.description:
The `GET /refunds/{refundId}` response: the recorded refund + its clearing
state (Group G). Drawn from the `refund` row (the surrogate `(tenant,
refund_id)` grain). `clearing_state` is the two-stage `REFUND_CLEARING` drain
state (`PENDING` ⇒ stage-1 open / `SETTLED` ⇒ drained or single-step /
`REVERSED` ⇒ a PSP reject/void line-negated the stage-1). Tenant-scoped
(SQL-level BOLA): an unknown refund — or one outside the caller's subtree —
yields a `404` (no existence leak).

phase.description: The latest lifecycle phase recorded on this refund.

relates_to_refund_id.description: The refund-of-refund forward link (`None` for a first-order refund).

reverses_entry_id.description: The negated stage-1 entry id on a PSP reject/void (`None` otherwise).

RefundWithCreditNoteRequest.description:
The `POST /refund-with-credit-note` request body: post a refund AND its paired
S3 credit note ATOMICALLY in one transaction as two linked entries (K-3,
design §4.4). The refund carries the credit note's id (`credit_note_id`) so the
two are linked; AR is never overstated between them (both commit or neither).
The target seller ledger is the body's own `tenant_id`; the `(entry, post)` PEP
gate authorizes it. Carries BOTH the refund request and the credit-note request
inline (each its own idempotency grain) — a composite, not a discriminated
union.

credit_note.description: The paired S3 credit note to post atomically with the refund.

RefundWithCreditNoteResponse.description:
The `POST /refund-with-credit-note` response: references to BOTH posted entries
(the refund + the paired credit note), committed atomically. Always `201` on a
fresh composite (an idempotent replay of an already-posted composite renders
`200`; both halves replay together since they share the post txn).

credit_note_entry_id.description: The posted credit-note entry id (the paired second entry).

replayed.description: `true` ⇒ an idempotent replay of an already-posted composite (both halves).

RegisterEntitiesRequest.description: Request DTO for registering GTS entities.

entities.description: Array of GTS entities to register.

results.description: Results for each entity in the request.

RegisterResultDto.description: Result of registering a single entity.

oneOf.description: Successfully registered entity.
Failed to register entity.

gts_id.description: The GTS ID that was attempted, if available.

RegisterSummaryDto.description: Summary of a batch registration operation.

ReidentifyRequestDto.description:
`POST …/audit/reidentify` request body: the payer to re-identify + the
machine `reason_code`. The free-text `reason` is the **`X-Investigation-Reason`
header** (§5), not a body field; both reason and `reason_code` are required
(a missing one is rejected `MISSING_INVESTIGATION_REASON`).

target_scope.description:
The tenant whose PII map to re-identify against (defaults to the caller's
own). A different tenant is the forensic cross-tenant path (§5):
authorized for `(entry, reidentify)` on the target, else
`CROSS_TENANT_ACCESS_DENIED`.

ReidentifyResponseDto.description:
`POST …/audit/reidentify` response: the recovered opaque `pii_ref` (the
pointer into the external PII store; never the PII itself).

reason.description:
Why the change is refused. Blank is absent — a `reason` column holding a
space satisfies `chk_pricing_approval_reason` and tells an auditor
nothing.

assets.description:
The stored asset slice (`name`, `browser_download_url`, `size` per
asset), passed through as JSON; `[]` when the release has none.

lines.description:
The lines, **replaced and never merged**: every D-42 rule quantifies over
the set, so a partial update leaves nothing the validator can evaluate.

revision.description: The revision being edited. Must be the open draft.

clone_url.description:
Always present: falls back to the canonical github.com URL when the
row was mirrored before the column existed.

node_id.description: GitHub's GraphQL global id, as GitHub itself returns it.

RepricingAdjustmentRequest.description:
What the run does to every selected row's amount.

The four members are [`OverlayLineRequest`]'s, spelled identically and parsed
by [`crate::domain::overlay::adjustment_of`] — the same function, not a copy. `inst-mr-api` names the
adjustment without defining it, and a second vocabulary for "what to do to a
price" is the hazard the overlay plane's own line parser already exists to
prevent.

[`OverlayLineRequest`]: crate::api::rest::overlays::OverlayLineRequest

adjustment_value.description: The basis-points magnitude, on a `percent_bp` adjustment.

amounts.description: The per-currency values, on an `amount` adjustment.

RepricingJournalRowView.description: One selected row and how far it got (`inst-mr-journal`).

applied_price_id.description: The successor the apply created. Present exactly on `applied`.

failure_reason.description: Why it did not apply. Present exactly on `failed`.

price_id.description: The published row this run selected.

state.description:
`pending | applied | failed`.

**`not-attempted` is not among them.** D-261 makes that a *rendering* of a
`pending` row on a report, never a stored value, which is what lets a
re-drive tell "never reached" from "decided" — for a run left
`committing` after an ordinary apply failure, where a row reading
`pending` here genuinely means "not yet reached, retake the lock and
carry on". A run a panic or a dropped future ended instead reaches a
terminal state with every such row marked `failed`
(`infra::repricing::RunLockGuard`'s `Drop` fallback, which has no code
left running to preserve the distinction any other way) — there,
"never reached" survives only in `failure_reason`'s free text, not in
this field.

adjustment.description: What to do to their amounts.

changeover.description:
**One** instant for every row of the run (D-88). Strictly future at
submit; the approval commit holds it to a whole batching delay.

run_id.description:
The caller's name for this run, and §5's idempotency column for the
surface. It becomes the run's `client_key`, so a second `POST` under it
answers the run it opened rather than opening a second one.

selector.description: Which published rows to act on.

RepricingRunView.description: A run and its journal — `inst-mr-return`'s progress endpoint, whole.

completed_at.description: When it ended; absent while it is still going.

journal.description: The frozen row set, in `price_id` order.

operation_id.description:
The run's durable row name, and what the journal's own `run_id` column
holds. Both are on the view because they are two different values.

report.description:
The frozen run parameters — selector, adjustment, changeover, and how many
rows the expansion found.

run_id.description: The caller's `run_id`, which is what the `GET` is addressed by.

state.description:
One of §4's seven states. A run this arm opened has already left
`validating`, for `awaiting_approval` or `committing` on its materiality
verdict, and is at that state when the `POST` answers — the apply runs after
the response, so the terminal state is the `GET`'s to report.

RepricingSelectorRequest.description:
Which published rows the run acts on: any subset of the canonical key's axes.

**Spelled as [`ScopeKeyRequest`] spells them**, field for field, with two
differences that are both the difference between a key and a filter: every
member is optional, because an absent axis is one the run does not constrain;
and the usage pair `(meter, dimensionKey)` is here, because D-196 authors that
pair on a row's *content* while a selector is choosing among rows already
filed under it.

`plan_id` is a member rather than a path segment for
[`BulkImportRowRequest`](crate::api::rest::bulk_imports::BulkImportRowRequest)'s
reason: a run may span plans, and `pricing_bulk_operation` carries a tenant and
no plan.

[`ScopeKeyRequest`]: crate::api::rest::prices::ScopeKeyRequest

cohort.description:
Axis 8: the grandfathering generation's cutover instant.

`null` is **unconstrained** here, where on
[`ScopeKeyRequest`](crate::api::rest::prices::ScopeKeyRequest) it is *a row
that retains nobody*. The second meaning is not lost: `cohort != none` if
and only if `priceEligibility == existing_grandfathered`, so the rows that
retain nobody are selected through `price_eligibility` instead.

currency.description: Axis 2, ISO 4217 — §2's *"a currency segment"* is this member alone.

dimension_key.description:
Axis 10 (D-196). The empty string selects the **undimensioned** rows,
whose column holds the empty-tuple sentinel rather than a `NULL`.

**Absent and `""` are different runs, and no read surface emits the
second.** Absent leaves the axis unconstrained — every dimension of the
meter — while `""` constrains it to the rows carrying no dimension at all.
A price read renders an undimensioned line as `null` on both members that
carry it, so an operator composing a selector from a row they just read
gets the *unconstrained* run unless they author the empty string here
deliberately. The overloading is this field's, not the read's: one member
cannot both name a value and mean "do not filter" without a spelling that
no absence renders as.

phase.description:
Axis 5. Axis 4, `priceOverlay`, is absent by construction: every row this
gear authors is on the `base` plane.

plan_id.description:
Axis 1. Absent selects across plans; named, it is also the axis D-134
groups the apply's transactions by.

price_eligibility.description:
Axis 6 — `all_subscriptions | new_subscriptions_only |
existing_grandfathered`.

**The one axis whose absence narrows the run rather than widening it.**
Leaving it out excludes `existing_grandfathered`
(`inst-mp-grandfathered`); naming it is how an operator asks for that
class, and what they then get is the per-row refusal the apply owes.

RequestChildConversionDto.description:
Request body for `POST /tenants/{tenant_id}/child-conversions`
(initiator = parent acting on a direct child). Same field set as
[`RequestOwnConversionDto`] plus the explicit `child_tenant_id`
because the URL binds the parent — the converting child has to be
identified in the body.

comment.description:
Optional caller-supplied rationale. Same `1..=1000` chars
contract as [`RequestOwnConversionDto::comment`].

RequestOwnConversionDto.description:
Request body for
`POST /tenants/{tenant_id}/conversions` (initiator = converting
tenant). `target_mode` is REQUIRED — the service rejects any value
other than the strict binary inverse of the tenant's current
`self_managed` flag with `code=validation`. `comment` is optional
(1..=1000 chars when supplied; empty strings are a contract bug and
surface as `code=validation`).

comment.description:
Optional caller-supplied rationale. The service rejects
`Some("")` and any value over 1000 chars with
`code=validation` BEFORE the DB write. The `min_length` /
`max_length` constraints below advertise the same contract
to the served `OpenAPI` so codegen clients see the bound
statically rather than discovering it via a runtime 400.

reason.description: Operator / Finance reason (audit context; recorded with the actor).

ResolvedTenantMetadataDto.description:
Effective-value resolution result for the inheritance-aware walk-up
surface.

`resolved == false` carries no `value` — the terminal empty state
of an `OverrideOnly` schema, a `self_managed` barrier, or a walk
that reached the root without a hit. Distinct from
`metadata_entry_not_found` (which only fires on the single-entry
`GET` path); `resolve` always returns HTTP 200 per FEATURE §3.

id.description: Specific resource ID (for GET/UPDATE/DELETE on a single resource).

properties.description: Additional resource properties for policy evaluation.

ResourceRefDto.description:
Wire-projection of [`usage_collector_sdk::ResourceRef`]. Mirrors the SDK
shape verbatim; the SDK struct stays `utoipa`-free.

ResubmitRequest.description:
A resubmit body carrying the preparer's edited intent (the stored `intent`
jsonb shape). The kind cannot change; the approval returns to `PENDING`.

RetentionRuleBodyDto.description:
Retention rule body in requests and responses.

@cpt-cf-file-storage-fr-retention-policies

RetireBody.description: The body of a retirement request.

dry_run.description:
Preview only: compute the verdict, write nothing, open no unit.

**Defaults to the safe arm.** A body that omits it is read as a dry-run,
because the failure modes are not symmetric: a caller who meant to confirm
and got a preview reads it and calls again, while a caller who meant to
preview and got a confirm has opened an approval unit over an irreversible
act.

oneOf.description: The unit a second principal has to decide. `null` on the committed arm.

cancelled_window_ids.description:
The windows the cancellation flow was invoked on. Empty on the controlled
arm, and empty on the committed one too whenever the presence lane could
not answer.

pending_version_ref.description:
The registry's pending handle. `null` on the controlled arm: no version is
requested for an act that did not commit (D-156).

preview.description: What was decided about, on both arms — the approver reads it here.

blocking_references.description:
References that **block** the retirement. Non-empty means the confirm
would be refused `RETIRE_PLAN_REFERENCED`.

presence_unresolved.description:
Whether the in-flight-subscriber lane could be asked at all.

`true` says every window above is kept because nobody could be asked
rather than because a subscriber was found — D-131's fail-closed clause,
which D-182 makes this system's only case.

revision.description: The revision the flip would target.

windows.description: Every not-yet-active window, and what would happen to it.

ReturnPaymentRequest.description:
The `POST /payments/{payment_id}/returns` request body: claw a settled
receipt back out (the reversal of a money-in). `{payment_id}` (the original
settled payment) comes from the PATH; `psp_return_id` is the idempotency key
(a re-post replays). `scale` is advisory; `effective_at` `None` ⇒ stamped at
post time.

effective_at.description: Return instant; `None` ⇒ stamped at post time (current-month period).

psp_return_id.description: External return identity — the idempotency key.

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this returns within; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

ReturnPaymentResponse.description:
The `POST /payments/{payment_id}/returns` response: a reference to the return
posting. A fresh return renders `201`, an idempotent replay `200` (the
handler reads `replayed`).

RevShareGroupRequest.description: One rev-share group of a submitted composition.

platform_cut_bp.description: The group's explicit platform cut, in basis points.

residual_absorber_party.description:
Who absorbs the publish-time residual — a party of this group, or the
`platform` sentinel. Absent means `platform`, which is D-07's default and
what makes an unnominated state unrepresentable.

vendor_sku_id.description: The included vendor SKU whose revenue this group allocates.

RevaluationRunRequest.description:
Trigger an unrealized (Mode-B) revaluation for one period across the monetary
scopes `{AR, UNALLOCATED, REUSABLE_CREDIT}` (design §4.5). `tenant_id` rides
the body (the vhp-core write convention). Each scope is idempotent on
`(tenant, period_id, scope)` — re-posting the same period replays the
already-posted scopes. A no-op when the tenant is Mode-A
(`revaluation_enabled = false`).

period_id.description:
The period to revalue (`YYYYMM`). Must be an OPEN period at run time (the
run posts INTO it); a CLOSED/absent period is rejected by the posting gate.

tenant_id.description: The seller tenant whose foreign-currency monetary positions are remeasured.

RevaluationRunResponse.description: The outcome of a revaluation run — one entry per monetary scope.

RevaluationScopeOutcomeDto.description:
One monetary scope's revaluation outcome (aggregated across its per-payer
entries — an entry spans only one payer, so a scope fans out over payers).

entries.description: Entries freshly written this call (a full idempotent replay reports `0`).

grains.description: Grains moved across those entries (a forward run only; `0` for a no-op).

status.description:
The outcome: `posted` (entries written), `nothing_to_post` (no
cross-currency movement / a full idempotent replay), or `disabled` (Mode A).

RevenueDisaggregationEntryDto.description:
One disaggregated recognized-revenue grain in the `GET
/revenue/disaggregation` response: the revenue RECOGNIZED into
`revenue_stream` during `period_id` (`Σ amount_minor` of the DONE recognition
segments at that grain), in minor units of `currency`. A row of
[`RevenueDisaggregationResponse::entries`].

currency.description: ISO currency of the recognized amount.

period_id.description: The fiscal period the revenue recognized in (`YYYYMM`).

recognized_minor.description: Revenue recognized into this `(period, stream)` grain, in minor units.

revenue_stream.description: The revenue stream the recognized revenue books to.

RevenueDisaggregationResponse.description:
The `GET /revenue/disaggregation` response: recognized ASC 606 revenue
disaggregated by `(period_id, revenue_stream)`, ordered by
`(period_id, revenue_stream)`. NOTE: like `ar-aging`, this is a **computed
aggregate report** (a grouped SUM over the recognized segments), not a
paginated row collection — it keeps plain `?tenant_id=&period_id=` query
params (no `OData` `$filter` / `Page` envelope).

ReversalRequestDto.description:
The `POST /journal-entries/{entryId}/reversals` request body. The reversed
entry is the `{entryId}` path id; the tenant is the caller's auth context.
The reversal lands in the supplied `period_id` (a still-OPEN period — it may
differ from the original's) effective `effective_at`; both default
server-side to the original's period / today when omitted.

effective_at.description: GL effective date of the reversal; `None` ⇒ today (UTC).

period_id.description: Target OPEN period for the reversal; `None` ⇒ the original's period.

reason.description: Audit reason for the reversal (recorded by the caller's actor).

line.description:
GitHub's current diff anchors, which its own UI positions inline
comments by; `position` above is the deprecated form.

original_position.description:
Line position at comment-creation time — the stable anchor across
later force-pushes.

position.description:
Line position in the current diff; absent once GitHub considers the
commented-on line outdated.

pull_request_review_id.description: The review this inline comment belongs to, as GitHub reports it.

ReviewThreadDto.description: A mirrored PR review conversation thread, served by the extended API.

resource.description:
What this document is a representation **of**.

A constant, and it exists for a client rather than for a reader: a
response carries no URL, so a client that must pair this body with the
`ETag` header — the only source of the `PUT`'s precondition — has nothing
else to attribute it by. `taxonomies::TaxonomyView` already discriminates
on `class`; these two documents were structurally identical (`values`
alone) and a client reading several config documents concurrently could
pair either one's tag with the other's body, which is a wrong
precondition rather than a failed one.

values.description:
Every declared value, `active` and `retired` alike, ordered by value.

Retirements are **included** so the round trip is honest: an operator who
reads, edits and writes back can see the value they are about to
re-activate.

state.description:
`active` or `retired`. Absent reads as `active`, because a body listing a
value is a body declaring it.

value.description: The reference a price row's `roundingPolicyRef` must match. Never blank.

default_rounding_policy_ref.description: The reference, or `null` when the tenant has set no default.

ScheduleChangeResponse.description:
The `POST /recognition-schedules/{schedule_id}/changes` response: a small
reference to the change's outcome. `new_schedule_id` is the successor version's
id on a `replace` (`null` on a `cancel`); `status` is the original schedule's
resulting status (`"REPLACED"` | `"CANCELLED"`). Always `200` (the change is
applied or an idempotent replay).

new_schedule_id.description: The successor schedule version's id on a `replace`; `null` on a `cancel`.

schedule_id.description: The original schedule that was cancelled / replaced.

ScheduleMigrationBody.description: The body of a scheduling request.

effective_at.description:
When the migration takes effect. Validated against the tenant's notice
period (D-49) with a 60-day floor.

migration_id.description:
**Client-supplied, and the idempotency key** (M2, `inst-ms-api`).

Required rather than minted server-side: a timed-out client must be able
to retry and get the original schedule back, which is only possible if the
client chose the identity. Mirrors Slice 12's `run_id`.

scope.description:
`all` or a subscription filter. Free-form, because the catalog does not
interpret it — it rides the `PlanMigrationScheduled` contract to the party
that does.

target_plan_id.description: The target. MUST be a published plan (`inst-mg-target`).

ScheduleWindowRequest.description:
The body of `POST /prices/{priceId}/windows`.

`effectiveTo` is `Option` and its absence means **open-ended**, which is the
store's own reading: a window with no end covers every instant from its start.
It is deliberately not a required field with a sentinel — an open-ended window
is the ordinary case for a plan's first window, and a sentinel instant would be
an instant somebody eventually compares against.

effective_from.description:
Inclusive start, UTC, strictly in the future (`inst-ws-future-start`,
D-63).

effective_to.description: Exclusive end, UTC; absent is open-ended.

reason_code.description: Why the window was scheduled — free text the store keeps with the row.

ScopeKeyRequest.description:
The six axes a caller authors. The stored key is ten: `planId` is the path
segment, `priceOverlay` is always `base` on this plane, and the usage pair is
derived from the row's content (D-196 clause (3)).

`price_overlay` is **not** a member: every row this gear authors carries
`base`, and partner / orgTier / brand overlays are separate overlay rows
rather than a value of this axis. Offering it would offer a choice the
authoring plane does not have.

`plan_id` is not a member either — it is the `{planId}` path segment, so a
body cannot name a plan the URL does not.

cohort.description:
The grandfathering generation's cutover instant, or `null` for a row
that retains nobody.

phase.description:
The phase this row prices; the plan's terminal phase for a
phase-invariant row (D-19).

ScopeKeyView.description:
The ten axes as the store holds them.

**Two more members than [`ScopeKeyRequest`], and the asymmetry is D-196's.**
The usage line is authored on the *content* view — a request naming it on the
key would be a second place to state one fact — so `ScopeKeyRequest` has no
`meter` and no `dimension_key`, while the key a row is **filed under** carries
both. This view is the store's rendering, not an echo of the request, and
rendering eight answers two rows on two meters of one market with
byte-identical `scope_key` objects — a reviewer reading the approval surface
sees one key twice and no way to tell which line they are approving.

cohort.description: Axis 8, `null` when the row retains nobody.

dimension_key.description:
Axis 10 — the dimension discriminator on the line, `null` for the
undimensioned one (D-196).

`null` rather than the store's `''` sentinel, for [`Self::cohort`]'s
reason: an empty string on the wire is a value a caller can read as one,
and "no dimension" is an absence. The sentinel is the column's business.

meter.description: Axis 9 — the metering unit, `null` on a row that is not metered (D-196).

price_overlay.description: Axis 4 — always `base` on an authored row.

SecretMetadataDto.description: Access metadata returned alongside the secret value.

is_inherited.description: Whether the secret came from an ancestor tenant.

owner_tenant_id.description: The tenant that owns this secret.

sharing.description: The sharing mode that governed the lookup result.

type.description: Secret type as its full GTS type id.

version.description: Monotonic version of the resolved secret (also returned as `ETag`).

ServiceAccountCreateRequestDto.description:
Request body for
`POST /account-management/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/service-accounts`.
`tenant_id` comes from the path.

`name` / `scopes` are not secret, so `Debug` is plain-derived —
unlike [`ServiceAccountCredentialsDto`] below, which hand-writes a
redacting one.

name.description:
Short caller-chosen name, unique among the tenant's live
accounts. Adapters commonly derive the client id as
`svc-<tenant_id>-<name>`, but that format is a convention rather
than contract; the listing echoes this `name` back so callers
correlate without parsing client ids. AM bounds the length; the
charset and uniqueness are the provider's to enforce.

scopes.description:
Client scopes to attach; validated against the provider's
allowlist.

ServiceAccountCredentialsDto.description:
Live credentials returned by create and rotate-secret.

The secret is returned ONLY here — there is no read-back endpoint.
`Debug` is hand-written to redact it, and both handlers set
`Cache-Control: no-store` so no intermediary retains the body.

client_id.description:
The provider-assigned client id, used to address rotate-secret
and revoke. Opaque to callers.

client_secret.description:
The `client_credentials` secret. Persist it immediately;
recovery from loss is a rotate, not a read.

subject_id.description:
The account's subject id (`sub` of issued tokens) — use it for
RBAC bindings.

token_url.description: OAuth token endpoint for the `client_credentials` grant.

client_id.description:
The provider-assigned client id, used to address rotate-secret
and revoke.

enabled.description: Whether the client can currently authenticate.

name.description:
The caller-supplied `name` this account was created with,
reported verbatim by the provider. This is how a caller
correlates a name it submitted with an opaque `client_id` —
notably to reconcile a create that returned `409`
`AMBIGUOUS_OUTCOME`.

scopes.description:
Attached client scopes as reported by the `IdP` — includes
realm-default scopes, not only the requested ones.

ServiceAccountListDto.description:
Response body for
`GET /account-management/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/service-accounts`.

Deliberately not a `toolkit_odata::Page` like the user listing: the
contract is unpaginated (the provider returns the tenant's whole
collection), because this listing is also the reconciliation path for
an ambiguous create — "is my name already live here?" must not be a
multi-round-trip question with a cursor to invalidate.

service_accounts.description: The tenant's service accounts, in provider order.

SetDualControlPolicyRequest.description:
A new dual-control threshold policy version to write (DC8). `effective_from`
defaults to now when omitted; out-of-range D2/A6/TTL is rejected (409, no clamp).

SetFxRevaluationModeRequest.description:
A new FX revaluation-mode version to write (VHP-1986). `effective_from`
defaults to now when omitted. An unknown `revaluation_mode` is rejected (400),
never coerced.

effective_from.description: When this version takes effect; defaults to now.

revaluation_mode.description:
`MODE_A` (defer the period-end revaluation to the tenant's ERP — the
fail-safe default) or `MODE_B` (BSS is the ledger of record and runs the
unrealized revaluation).

scope_owner_id.description: Target owner id (required when `scope = "user"`; omit for tenant scope).

SetPostingPolicyRequest.description:
A new posting-policy version to write (VHP-1853). `effective_from` defaults to
now when omitted. An unknown `missing_mapping_mode`, or empty / non-positive /
non-monotone `ar_aging_thresholds`, is rejected (400), never coerced.

ar_aging_thresholds.description:
AR-aging bucket upper-bounds: strictly increasing positive day counts
(e.g. `[30, 60, 90]` → `current / 1-30 / 31-60 / 61-90 / 90+`).

effective_from.description: When this version takes effect; defaults to now.

missing_mapping_mode.description:
`SUSPENSE` (route unmapped items to suspense — the default) or `HARD_BLOCK`
(reject a post that carries an unmapped item).

SetReactionReq.description: Request DTO for setting a reaction.

SettlePaymentRequest.description:
The `POST /payments` request body: a settled payment to record (the
**money-in** side). The target seller ledger is the body's own `tenant_id`
(tenant in body, not path — the vhp-core REST convention); the `(payment,
write)` PEP gate authorizes it. `scale` is the payment's currency scale as
known to the caller — advisory; the ledger resolves the authoritative
per-line scale from the provisioned currency config. `effective_at` `None`
⇒ the receipt is stamped at post time.

effective_at.description: Receipt instant; `None` ⇒ stamped at post time (current-month period).

fee_minor.description: Processor's withheld cut in minor units (`<= gross`).

gross_minor.description: Gross received in minor units (what the payer was charged).

payment_id.description: External payment identity — the idempotency key (a re-settle replays).

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this settles into; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

SettlePaymentResponse.description:
The `POST /payments` response: a reference to the settlement posting. A
fresh settle renders `201`, an idempotent replay `200` (the handler reads
`replayed`).

SettlementView.description:
The `GET /payments/{payment_id}/settlement` response: the per-payment money-out
serialization counters (read-surface R4). Drawn from the `payment_settlement`
row (the `(tenant, payment_id)` grain) — the settled / fee / allocated /
refunded / clawed-back running totals the money-out caps serialize against.
The persisted `version` (the optimistic-concurrency counter) is INTERNAL and
not surfaced. Tenant-scoped (SQL-level BOLA): a payment that was never settled
— or one outside the caller's subtree — yields a `404` (no existence leak).
Mirrors [`RefundView`].

allocated_minor.description: The portion of the pool already drained to open AR (money-out).

clawed_back_minor.description: The portion clawed back (a refund-of-refund / PSP claw-back).

fee_minor.description: The PSP fee withheld from the settled receipt.

refunded_minor.description: The portion already returned to the payer via refunds.

refunded_unallocated_minor.description: The portion refunded from the still-unallocated pool (Pattern A).

settled_minor.description: The gross settled amount recorded for the payment (money-in).

SharingModeDto.description: Sharing mode for the REST transport layer.

SizeLimitsDto.description: Size limits in a policy body.

max_bytes.description: Global maximum file size in bytes (`null` = unlimited at this level).

StreamEvent.description:
Stream event envelope for the `messages:stream` pipeline.

Each variant maps to a distinct SSE `event:` name and `data:` JSON payload.
Ordering grammar: `stream_started ping* (delta | tool)* citations? (done | error)`.

request_id.description: Client-generated idempotency key (UUID v4). Optional in P1.

oneOf.description: Web search configuration.

StreamStartedData.description:
Stream header event carrying the stream request ID and server-generated
assistant message ID.

Emitted as the first event in every SSE stream (both new generations and
replays). `is_new_turn` distinguishes replayed completed turns from live
generations.

is_new_turn.description:
`true` for a live generation (new turn); `false` when the stream
replays an already-completed turn (idempotent replay).

oneOf.description:
